_extraction_flags.notes: Survey paper - use for taxonomy reference and snowballing, not primary data

reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Figure 1-8: All diagrams show FIBER-based experimental setups. Key elements: 7-core SDM fiber (Fig.5), φ-OTDR/DAS backscatter sensing (Fig.6), DSCM with LFM pilots (Fig.8). No free-space or wireless elements visible.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: System: Fiber-ISAC (ISAC-OF). This is a REVIEW PAPER surveying multiple methods. Two main categories: (1) Forward Transmitted Light (SOP/Phase extraction), (2) Backscattered Light (Rayleigh/φ-OTDR/DAS). Integration via WDM, SDM, same-wavelength, data-frame structures, DSCM.
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Metrics from surveyed papers: 36.8 Tb/s DWDM + sensing, 380 km sensing range, 0.5m spatial resolution (scheme [29]), 200 Gbps DP-16QAM + 4m DAS resolution (DSCM). Table I provides structured comparison.
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: Type: REVIEW/SURVEY paper, not original research. Contribution: Taxonomy of Fiber-ISAC methods. Key Gap: All methods sense vibration only; multi-object sensing is a challenge. Backscatter limited by isolators on amplified links.

bibliographic.title: Recent Advancements and Challenges in Integrated Sensing and Communication in Optical Fiber

application.scenario_description: Submarine cables, urban metro fiber networks, pipeline monitoring, intrusion detection, earthquake sensing.

key_contribution.key_contribution: Comprehensive taxonomy of Fiber-ISAC (ISAC-OF) methods categorized by Forward Transmitted Light (SOP/Phase) vs Backscattered Light (WDM/SDM/Same-wavelength/DSCM).
key_contribution.gap_addressed: Lack of unified survey covering both forward and backscatter-based fiber ISAC approaches.

tradeoff.notes: Phase vs SOP: Phase has higher sensitivity, SOP has more robustness in noisy environments.
